name: Tagger
author: brodgar
description: Example addon (039-uniform-api): EVERYTHING YOU ATTACH TO A GAME OBJECT, THROUGH ONE COLLECTION. gob:overlay() is the one way to hang a thing on a gob and the one way to read what is already hanging there: :list() answers them all, :get(key) reads one, :add(key) attaches a BARE one, :remove(key) removes it. THE OVERLAY SAYS WHAT IT DRAWS, TWO SPACES -- :text(s) and :draw(fn) paint in SCREEN space at the gob's projected point (':tagger' puts a green name and a ring over every player body), while :image(a), :model(a) and :ghost(res) stand in the 3D WORLD anchored to the gob with a three-number :offset in world units (':tagger pin' floats icon.png 18 units over the nearest object in ONE chained statement, add(PIN):image(icon):scale(2):offset(0, 0, 18):tint(255, 200, 90):alpha(0.85)). Every setter answers the overlay and every one has a bare read, and an overlay that has not said what it draws paints nothing -- so a half-configured overlay never flickers. YOU NEVER PLACE IT AND YOU NEVER POLL IT: the record lives ON the gob, so it follows the gob for free and it DIES WITH IT -- a felled tree takes your label with it, and a gob that comes back is bare. THERE IS NO FILTER FORM, and this addon is what that trade looks like: 'label every player' is a GobAdded handler plus one loop over the players already here, so nothing is searched per frame. ':tagger read' is the other half of the read -- it prints yours (native = false, with a kind) beside THE GAME'S OWN (native = true, keyed by their resource name, read-only, and a union over that name, which is why ov:count() exists). ':tagger watch' turns on the two events, GobOverlayAdded and GobOverlayRemoved, which arrive on the next frame rather than inside the verb: yours owner-scoped, the game's broadcast. SAFE tier: declares no permissions, sends nothing to the server, writes nothing persistent, and everything it attached is gone on ':reload' or on disable.
